entries.title: Fish, Frog or Lizard? What Does a TADPOLE Become? (Part A)

moments.what: Round 1: what will the tadpole grow into?
Where do tadpoles come from? A frog lays eggs
Frog eggs in a clump of clear jelly, each dark dot an egg
Frog eggs have a jelly-like covering: it protects them and keeps them wet
Journey: be a frog egg, hatch into a tadpole and grow into a frog
The young of the frog is called a tadpole
A tadpole does not look like the adult frog
HOLD ON! Is a tadpole with legs a new stage? No: three stages
A life cycle with three stages: the egg, the young and the adult
A hen and her chicks: does every young animal look different?
Look at the body parts, not the colour: a chick looks like the adult
Some young animals look like their parents, while some do not

entries.title: Why Did This Grasshopper Leave Its SKIN Behind? (Part B)

moments.what: Round 1: a little grasshopper with no wings: young or adult?
A young grasshopper beside an adult: six legs, two feelers, no wings yet
A young grasshopper is called a nymph
The life cycle of a grasshopper has three stages
An empty grasshopper skin on the grass: why?
The outer skin is hard and cannot stretch, so it gets too tight
Journey: be the nymph, shed your skin and grow wings
Shedding the old outer skin to grow bigger is called moulting
As a young insect grows, it sheds its outer skin: moulting
Showdown: the cockroach's young looks like the adult
Cockroach eggs are found in an egg case
